I am a young woman here in Oromia, and this small plot of beans is important for my family's food and a little income. Beans fix their own nitrogen, so I don't waste my small money on chemical fertilizer for them — I save that for my maize on the bigger plots. I will spread some manure from our animals because the soil here is getting tired, and I will plant seeds I saved from last harvest since improved bean seed is expensive and not always available at our market. I have no irrigation, so I depend on the belg and meher rains, and since the plot is only a tenth of a hectare I can manage the weeding and harvest myself with help from my mother and sister.
